prompt: Which questions does Sônia ask before any dismissal at Caju? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Does the team want them to leave?
choices.why: No: the team’s preference is not one of the questions.

choices.text: Was the expectation clear, and when was it set?
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Is the manager sure?
choices.why: No: conviction is exactly what the questions replace with evidence.

choices.text: Is the person treated as others in the same situation would be?
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Was the support given?
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Under Brazil’s Law 12.506 of 2011, what notice does an employer owe on dismissal without cause?
hint: Thirty, plus a little per year, with a ceiling.

choices.text: Exactly thirty days
choices.why: Thirty is the base; the law adds three days per year of service.

choices.text: Thirty days plus three per year of service, up to ninety in total
choices.why: Right: and the people team, not the manager, explains what it means for the person.

choices.text: Ninety days in every case, whatever the length of service
choices.why: Ninety is the ceiling, not the rule.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Notice is owed on dismissal without cause.

prompt: Marcos had worked at Caju for three years. Under the rule of thirty days plus three per year of service, how many days of notice is that?
Why was Marcos’s access changed after the conversation rather than during it?

choices.text: Because the systems team was busy that morning
choices.why: It was planned that way on Sônia’s checklist.

choices.text: To spare him a locked laptop
choices.why: Right: the order of access and conversation is a matter of dignity.

choices.text: So he could finish his last ticket
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: Because the law requires access to remain open until the notice period has been fully worked
choices.why: The lesson gives dignity as the reason, not a legal rule.

prompt: Which of these is the manager’s to do, by the lesson?
hint: Not the terms, not the law.

choices.text: Negotiating the severance terms with the person in the meeting
choices.why: The manager does not negotiate the terms.

choices.text: Explaining the FGTS penalty
choices.why: The people team explains money, dates and rights.

choices.text: Deciding alone
choices.why: The decision was Renata’s, Sônia’s and Otávio’s together.

choices.text: The conversation
choices.why: Right: the decision is shared and the terms belong to the people team; the conversation is the manager’s.

prompt: Where does the decision come in the conversation, by the lesson?

choices.text: After a review of everything that went wrong, so the person understands why
choices.why: Over-explaining is for the manager’s comfort; the person already knows.

choices.text: At the end
choices.why: Leaving it to the end is burying it.

choices.text: In a message the day before
choices.why: The day before, Renata only said there would be a meeting.

choices.text: In the first minute
choices.why: Right: not after five minutes about the plan, and not phrased as a question.

prompt: Marcos says the last ticket was late because of a dependency on Payments. What does Renata do?

choices.text: Goes through the ticket’s history to show him he was responsible for the delay
choices.why: That is debating the decision, which the lesson says to avoid.

choices.text: Reconsiders
choices.why: The decision was made through the process before the meeting.

choices.text: Says the decision is made, without arguing about the ticket
choices.why: Right: arguing implies the decision is open; Sônia explains how to raise unfairness.

choices.text: Ends the meeting
choices.why: The rest of the time belongs to him.

prompt: Match each thing to avoid in the conversation with why it harms.

pairs.right: implies the decision is still open
serves the manager’s comfort, not the person

prompt: Instead of “this might be the best thing for you”, what did Renata say?

choices.text: That she was sure he would find something better soon
choices.why: That is the false comfort the lesson warns about.

choices.text: That she had fought hard for him with Otávio and Sônia but had been overruled in the end
choices.why: That would blame the others and imply disagreement with the decision.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: She said something true and specific.

choices.text: That his library documentation was good, and she would give a factual reference
choices.why: Right: specific, true, and useful to him.

prompt: What did Renata tell the team about why Marcos left?

choices.text: The plan and its result, so that the team would see that the process had been fair
choices.why: Seeing a fair process comes from months of experience, not from publishing his plan.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: sharing them would publish something private about somebody not there to respond.

choices.text: That he had resigned
choices.why: That would be untrue.

choices.text: That he was not a good fit
choices.why: A judgement about him, which she did not share.

prompt: Put what Renata did with the team in order.
hint: Same day, then the week after.
items: Told them in person, the same day, before systems showed the change
Answered the practical questions about work and on-call
Raised the unspoken worry in each one-to-one that week

prompt: Why could Renata honestly tell Thiago he had nothing to worry about?

choices.text: Because he was too junior to be dismissed
choices.why: Seniority does not protect anybody; the process does.

choices.text: The team had seen that nobody is dismissed without months of clear warning
choices.why: Right: a fair process makes the reassurance true rather than merely kind.

choices.text: Because she would never let it happen again on her team, whatever the circumstances
choices.why: That would be a promise she cannot make.

choices.text: Because Otávio said so
choices.why: The reason is what the team has seen.

prompt: When somebody is dismissed, the question in most people’s heads is “am I ___?”

A manager plans to tell an engineer on a Friday at 17:30, by video call, that their employment is ending, after their accounts have been disabled so nothing can be deleted. What would this lesson change first?

choices.text: Nothing, since disabling access first protects the company
choices.why: The lesson puts dignity first and changes access right after the conversation.

choices.text: The order: tell her first and change access afterwards, early in the week, and in person if that is possible
choices.why: Right: learning the news from a disabled account is the indignity Sônia’s checklist exists to prevent.

choices.text: Only the time, moving it to the morning
choices.why: The morning helps, but the order of access and conversation matters more.

choices.text: Sending a written letter instead of a call, so that she has everything in front of her at once
choices.why: A letter goes with the conversation; it does not replace it.
